title: Go-live conditions matrix and caution criteria
content:
Purpose:
This working doc encodes a compact, deterministic go/no-go conditions matrix and the associated caution criteria we should evaluate during preflight and the first 72 hours after go-live. Unlike long playbooks, this is intentionally terse for rapid decision-making in the activation war room.

How to use this doc:
- Owners: each row below has a primary and secondary owner. The primary is accountable for green/red at each gate.
- Gate cadence: preflight (T-3 days), final signoff (T-2 hours), 0h (deploy), +6h, +24h, +72h checks.
- If any red criteria are met, follow the rollback or mitigation clause in the right-hand notes.

1) Condition matrix (metric | green threshold | caution band | red trigger | owner | immediate action)
- API 95th latency (in ms) | < 220ms | 220-350ms | > 350ms sustained for 5m | Lucas Herrera | Throttle new sessions, enable lower-cost model variant, page SRE
- Error rate (5m request-weighted) | < 0.5% | 0.5% - 1.5% | > 1.5% or rising trend 30%/5m | Evan Green | Pause risky routes, enable degraded responses, open incident
- Token cost per 1k requests (estimated) | within -10% of forecast | -10% to +20% | > +20% vs forecast for 2 consecutive reporting windows | Priya Desai | Engage cost control policy, reduce batch size, review quantization profile
- Throughput (req/s) vs expected | > 95% of forecast | 80%-95% | < 80% or queuing growth | Lucas Herrera | Add dedicated capacity, failover to hosted pool
- Quality signal (eval set pass rate) | > 96% | 90%-96% | < 90% or drop >6pts | Maya Patel | Roll back model variant, block canary expansion, notify ML team
- Prefix cache hit ratio | > 70% | 50%-70% | < 50% | Evangeline (Cache eng) | Flush / investigate cache warmup, apply cache hints
- Observability ingest health | all streams gold | one stream degraded | multiple streams failing | SRE lead | Start logging failover, preserve samples to S3

2) Caution criteria (soft red) - things to watch but not immediate rollback
- New-to-product user complaints exceeding baseline by 2x but metrics still green -> hold marketing ramp, increase CS staffing.
- Small but consistent uptick in tail latency (p99) without p95 movement -> schedule deeper perf tracing run, do not expand traffic slice.
- Cost drift localized to single customer or route -> throttle or apply per-customer limits before global changes.

3) Staged rollout gating logic (how canaries expand)
- Stage A (internal + 5% alpha): require all green for 2h continuous.
- Stage B (beta 50%): require green for 6h and no red triggers in last 30m.
- Stage C (open): green for 24h and cost within forecast bounds for last 12h.
If any red during expansion -> immediate stop and roll back to previous traffic slice.

4) Preflight checklist (T-3 days -> T-1 hour condensed):
- Final model pinned + checksum verified (ml-oncall)
- Capacity stress test complete at 2x expected burst (infra)
- Tracing hooks and sample retention configured for 72h (observability)
- Canary auto-scaling policies verified and cooldown set to 2m (platform)
- Access and escalation roster distributed to war room doc (product-ops)
- Runbook snippets for the top 5 likely failures attached to pager messages (SRE)
- Customer-facing messaging draft ready if outage needed (CS + comms)

5) War room quick commands (copy-paste ops):
- Pause canary expansion: /deploy pause-canary --id=LAUNCH-123
- Throttle heavy routes: /router set-rate /generate 20rps --scope=customer
- Swap model to fallback: /models switch active=redwood-approx-quant
- Snapshot logs for ML debugging: /obs snapshot --window=5m --tag=LAUNCH-123

6) Rollback decision rubric (minimal list):
- Any red on "Quality signal" persisting > 15m -> full rollback to previous model version.
- Error rate red + sustained growth -> rollback unless can isolate to a single route/customer.
- Observability streams loss + unknown failure mode -> pause expansion and degrade to read-only mode for 30m while preserving samples.

7) Postmortem / immediate follow-ups (first 72h)
- Collect 3 canonical example requests that failed with timestamps + traces.
- Cost variance report every 24h until stable.
- Customer-impacting incidents: notify legal and security if data exposure suspected.

8) Quick owner contact roster (primary / secondary / pager)
- Product Ops: Maya Patel / Evan Green / pager: #prodops-ww-page
- SRE: Lucas Herrera / Jin Sou / pager: #sre-oncall
- ML: Priya Desai / Omar Rizvi / pager: #ml-oncall
- Observability: Evangeline Wu / Harpreet Kaur / pager: #obs-oncall

Notes and open questions (working):
- Should we add a KL-divergence check on responses vs baseline for novelty detection? (ml team)
- Decide whether cost alert uses tokenized estimate or actual billing - currently both; prefer near-real-time estimate for runbook gating.
- Validate that the fallback model has identical API semantics for structured tool-calls.

Last updated by Maya Patel 2025-11-20 — next review scheduled before next major launch.
